column1: # libOsiris.so shipped with bg3 4.1.1.7398727 (Steam build 24532579, bg3 build-id c8da62b1…); snapshot $BG3_SPECIMENS/steam-24532579_c8da62b137caebd03b57c23b65ba2547745ce851/bin/libOsiris.so
# The second module's manifest: the Osiris globals upstream reads off COsiris::COsiris (OsirisStaticGlobals),
# named as upstream names them, with Osiris's own names (the macOS libOsiris.dylib exports them) in the note. All in .bss.
# Witness for the ten: COsiris::COsiris 0x7c880 allocates and stores them in this order with these sizes, and the macOS
# constructor (0x4a950 in the x86_64 slice) does the same, size for size, into the named globals. The loader finds this
# module by soname (manifest::load_library) and verifies the rows against it like the game's own.

column7: OsiStringTable: 1st store of the ctor, an 8-byte object COsiStringTable::COsiStringTable (0x72c30) is called on; sits after COsiris::OsirisObject 0x111690 and s_Allocator 0x111698 as on macOS
RuleVariableMan: 2nd store, 0x1820 bytes = 256 x 24-byte items + count + an 0x800 buffer (upstream's VariableDb)
OsiDIVObjectTypesMan: 3rd store, 0x6008 bytes = 1023 x 24-byte libc++ map slots + NumItems + a 24-byte alias vector (OsiTypeDb)
OsiParseSymtableMan: 4th store, 0x28 bytes; the ctor then registers "__GLOBAL_SYMTABLE" in it (EnumDb)

OsiFunctionMan: 5th store, 0xc020 bytes = name index (1023 slots), id index (1023 slots), an id tree, an unordered_map, a counter; COsiris::GetFunctionMappings 0x8f7c0 walks its name index (stride 0x18 from +0x10, NumItems at +0x5fe8, counter at +0xc018)
OsiDIVObjectsMan: 6th store, 0xbff0 bytes = two 1023-slot indexes + a tree (ObjectDb)
OsiGoalMan: 7th store, 0x6008 bytes = 1023 slots + NumItems + a vector given a 0x1000-byte buffer (GoalDb)
ReteAdaptorFactory: 8th store, 0x20 bytes zeroed = {u32 Size; std::vector Elements} (TypedDb); copied to 0x119ec8 (PCFactoryProduct<CReteAdaptor>::s_pMyFactory)
ParserFlags: the dword COsiris::SetOption 0x8f420 reads, masks with upstream's DebugFlag bits (0x1ff0000, 0x100000, 0x4) and writes back; the log stream follows at 0x119d60 (fh_Log), as on macOS
